Admonish

ad-MON-ish · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To admonish is to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly.

The officer admonished the driver and let him go with a warning.

Worked Example

The captain admonished the young sailor to double-check every knot before the storm hit.

A firm, serious warning meant to correct behavior before something goes wrong is exactly what admonish describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

caution: warn someone about a possible danger or mistake

reprimand: express firm, formal disapproval

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

encourage: give support or confidence to

praise: express approval

Where it sits · how stern and official the warning — remind → admonish → reprimand

remind vs. admonish: To remind is neutral; to admonish is to firmly warn or reprimand, with a clear note of disapproval.

reprimand vs. admonish: Reprimand goes further than admonish, often implying a more formal, official rebuke.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ad-

prefix — ad-: to, toward (Latin)

root — mon

root — mon: to warn (Latin (monere))

suffix — -ish

suffix — -ish: verb-forming ending (Old French)

Put it together

Put it together: ad- ('toward') + mon ('to warn') + -ish together mean 'to warn toward' someone -- exactly the firm caution admonish describes.

Use the root in a new word: monitor

Use the root in a new word: monitor: Monitor comes from the same Latin root, monere ('to warn'), now used for something that watches and warns of problems.
